name: FeraSign
author: feradel

sections.description:
FeraSign connects your WordPress site to Feradel’s hosted electronic signature service. Select a published template approved for WordPress, configure how to identify the signer, and place the signing experience on a page with the FeraSign block or a shortcode.

  • Create and reuse signing configurations for approved templates.
  • Map eligible template fields to selected WordPress content, user fields, or supported form submissions.
  • Let signers read and complete documents on the embedded FeraSign screen or open the secure FeraSign page when sign-in is required.
  • Verify completion with FeraSign before running a follow-up workflow in WordPress.

A Feradel account with access to FeraSign is required. Feradel offers free and paid service plans. Available templates, signature volume, and retention depend on the service plan. The plugin is distributed under the GPL.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate FeraSign.
  2. Go to Settings > FeraSign. Choose Start Free or Connect Existing Account, then approve the connection on Feradel.
  3. In FeraSign, publish a template and approve it for WordPress.
  4. In Settings > FeraSign, create a configuration for the template. Set the signer identity and map any fields you want to prefill.
  5. Insert the FeraSign block and select your configuration, or paste the shortcode shown in Settings > FeraSign into a Shortcode block. Use an HTTPS page for signing.
  6. Preview with a test signer before sharing the page.
sections.faq:
What external service does this plugin use?

The plugin uses FeraSign for site authorization, template discovery, signing sessions, completion checks, and diagnostics. Your WordPress site connects to the FeraSign API at https://api.sign.feradel.com. The signing screen is served from https://sign.feradel.com. If you choose Start Free, your browser opens Feradel’s signup page.

What is sent to Feradel?

When a site administrator starts or manages the connection, WordPress sends site and installation identifiers, site URLs, and authorization information to Feradel. Once connected, the plugin sends the template and signing configuration information needed to start sessions. During a configured signing workflow, it sends the signer’s name and email, the permitted prefill values you mapped from WordPress, and request or session identifiers needed to track progress. Visitors interact directly with FeraSign to review and sign. Feradel stores signatures, executed documents, and the signing audit record.

See Feradel’s Terms of Use and Privacy Policy.

What information stays in WordPress?

WordPress stores connection settings and signing configurations. If you capture form submissions, WordPress retains them for 30 days by default. Signing request records contain reference IDs, status, timestamps, the initiating WordPress user ID when available, and a keyed hash of the signer’s email for privacy requests. The daily cleanup removes request records after 30 days.

The WordPress privacy tools can export or erase form submissions associated with a registered account. They can also export or erase local request records for the signer, including guest signers, or for the initiating WordPress user. Signing documents and the signing audit trail are managed in FeraSign. See the FeraSign product help for setup and support.

Where is the plugin source code?

The plugin package includes the complete, editable PHP, JavaScript, CSS, and SVG source. You can read and modify those files directly. The plugin has no compilation step.
sections.changelog:
1.0.14

  • Supports database setups with shorter index limits and retries incomplete schema upgrades.
  • Minimizes data in local request records and adds automatic expiry and WordPress privacy controls for them.
  • Requires a WordPress nonce for the browser connection callback and explicitly checks permissions on signing status and connection routes.

1.0.13

  • Initial submission to the WordPress Plugin Directory.
  • Uses the standard WordPress update mechanism and documents the data exchanged with the hosted FeraSign service.
